notes: HOW SHE HOLDS THE SEAT: Darline Graham (also reported as Darline Graham Nordone) is the sister of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham. Per Live 5 News (https://www.live5news.com/2026/07/14/darline-graham-sworn-interim-us-senator/, page opened), Gov. Henry McMaster appointed her interim senator on Monday 13 July 2026 after her brother's death, and she was sworn in on Tuesday 14 July 2026 to serve the remainder of his term; the article says she "will serve until Jan. 3, 2027, when the new Congress convenes." Sen. Tim Scott's release dated 14 July 2026 confirms the swearing-in date (https://www.scott.senate.gov/?p=22368, page opened). The date of Lindsey Graham's death was not stated on the pages I opened; a linked report was dated 12 July 2026, so treat that date as unconfirmed. IS SHE LEAVING IN JANUARY 2027: Yes, as far as sources show. She won the Republican nomination for the next six-year term in a special runoff on 25 August 2026 over Rep. Ralph Norman (https://www.newsfromthestates.com/article/darline-graham-wins-gop-nomination-next-us-senate-term-following-her-brothers-death, page opened), but lost the 3 November 2026 general election to Democrat Annie Andrews. The Associated Press projected Andrews the winner (about 50.6% to 47.2% at the time of the call), and the winner's term runs from 3 January 2027 (https://www.wbtv.com/2026/11/04/democrat-annie-andrews-wins-us-senate-seat-south-carolina-ap-projects/, page opened; also https://www.newsfromthestates.com/article/sc-elects-first-democrat-us-senate-28-years-stunning-win-over-trumps-pick, page opened). This is a media projection from election night; I did not see a certified result. No source I opened states her departure date outright after the election; it follows from the appointment ending on 3 January 2027 and her election loss. AI FINDINGS: None of the searches returned any statement, bill, letter or hearing remark by her about AI. Search results about 'Graham' and AI on senate.gov (for example the DEFIANCE Act releases) concern Lindsey Graham and were not attributed to her. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (S. 5493, Sanders): no source shows her as a co-sponsor, but I could not verify the co-sponsor list: congress.gov returned an error (HTTP 403) and the Sanders summary document could not be read as text. 23 September 2026 China letter: reports describe the 17 signers as Democrats; I did not see the full signer list. LIMITS OF THIS SEARCH: I could not find or open an official senate.gov site for her; the site-restricted search returned no page of hers. An Axios article of 16 September 2026 on lawmakers' AI use (https://www.axios.com/2026/09/16/lawmakers-regulate-ai-without-using-it) appeared in results but could not be opened (HTTP 403), so I do not know whether she is mentioned. The session's web search allowance ran out after eleven searches, so two further planned searches (the bill's co-sponsor list and her official site) were not run.
